name: Maximum width
description: Your classmate, whom you do not like because he is boring, but whom you respect for his intellect, has two strings: $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$ and $$$t$$$ of length $$$m$$$. A sequence $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_m$$$, where $$$1 \leq p_1 \lt p_2 \lt \ldots \lt p_m \leq n$$$, is called beautiful , if $$$s_{p_i} = t_i$$$ for all $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$. The width of a sequence is defined as $$$\max\limits_{1 \le i \lt m} \left(p_{i + 1} - p_i\right)$$$. Please help your classmate to identify the beautiful sequence with the maximum width . Your classmate promised you that for the given strings $$$s$$$ and $$$t$$$ there is at least one beautiful sequence.
input_specification: The first input line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \leq m \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the lengths of the strings $$$s$$$ and $$$t$$$. The following line contains a single string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$, consisting of lowercase letters of the Latin alphabet. The last line contains a single string $$$t$$$ of length $$$m$$$, consisting of lowercase letters of the Latin alphabet. It is guaranteed that there is at least one beautiful sequence for the given strings.
output_specification: Output one integer — the maximum width of a beautiful sequence.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1492C — Maximum width [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
